cases.name: Irene Blase
cases.narrative:
On 4/8/1969, she was discovered face-down in four feet of water in Saddle River, NJ, strangled with the chain from a crucifix she was wearing. 

Cottingham confessed that he saw Blase shopping in Hackensack and convinced her to join him for a drink. Taking a cab to another location, Cottingham and Blase spent time together after which Cottingham offered to bring Blase back to the bus station. He then drove Blase to a remote location against her will before raping and killing her.

cases.name: Latrice "Trice" Samara Avery
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Raised in Paterson, NJ, Trice fondest memories were from her childhood growing up on Barnert Place with her siblings and parents. Here is where Trice vivacious personality and her ability to make people around her laugh and smile was organically mastered.

Latrice graduated from John F. Kennedy High School in 1994. After graduating from high school Latrice attended the Business Training Institute with her dear friend, Kimberly where she studied to be a Certified Medical Assistant which began her career and desire to help others.

Latrice was employed with Casio Watch Co. and Shop-Rite where she was able to use her smile to engage her customers and provide quality customer service to all whom she came in contact with. She thrived in performing her job to the highest standard all while delivering the service with a smile.

Trice’s favorite color was green and this was befitting of her personality as the color green symbolizes creativity, it represents originality, it gives an emotional response of safety which was easily felt in her presence and it promotes a healing power which is necessary at this time. Green is also the color of the heart chakra. It governs emotions, compassion, love, truth and forgiveness and these traits perfectly embodied Trice.

Trice was a very gifted person however she was passionate about sewing and making clothes, listening to music, talking on the phone often saying “I just want to hear your voice”, always checking on friends and family, having a good time and laughing most of all. However; the true loves of her life were her sons Timothy “TJ” and William.

If you know Trice you felt her love. Trice was the epitome of the Nelson Mandela quote, “remember to smile”. For Trice smiling did not mean life was perfect, it was her symbol of hope and strength. All whom loved her dearly will never forget her wit, charm, and undying love for life and others. Trice will be deeply missed but we honor her life and the memories she left behind."
